headline: Wang Xingxing, founder of the Chinese robot maker Unitree, said at a Shanghai industry fair on 12 Oct that robots driven by AI could reach their tipping point within one to two years.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: the remarks were made on 12 Oct 2026 and match the headline, but they are a forecast with no new test data.
importance_line: A leading robot-company founder says AI-driven robots may become practical within one to two years, which, if right, would reach factory and service workers and the companies planning to buy robots, but it is one executive's forecast, from a company that sells robots, with no new figures behind it.
summary: BigGo Finance reports that Wang Xingxing, chairman and chief technology officer of Unitree Robotics, told the opening ceremony of the 26th China International Industry Fair in Shanghai on 12 Oct 2026 that, as AI models improve quickly, the tipping point for embodied intelligence (AI that controls physical machines such as robots) may arrive within one to two years, and that Unitree has put GPT-6 on various robots with results that have been “very impressive.” He acknowledged that factory pilots by Chinese and foreign companies still need to solve two problems, generalization (handling varied tasks) and efficiency, which he expects to be solved within a few years, and he expects commercial service uses to arrive before industrial ones and homes later.
notes: Read in full via BigGo Finance (fulltext); BigGo credits no other outlet and its quotes are translated. A forecast, so machine_action is false. BigGo's closing paragraph about investment effects is its own commentary and is not used. Headline-only Google News listings suggest Wang gave longer timelines in Aug and Sep 2026; not verified.
